record.paper_title: Challenges of Symbolic Computation: My Favorite Open Problems
record.original_question: For integers n ≥ 6 and positive real parameter r, eliminate the quantifiers and solve on a computer the minimax approximation problem of finding a polynomial B(x) = b0 + ··· + bn−2 x^(n−2) of degree at most n−2 that minimizes, over x in [−1, 1], the maximum absolute error |x^n + r x^(n−1) − B(x)|.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $n \ge 6$ and a positive real parameter $r > 0$, consider the Chebyshev-type minimax approximation problem on the interval $[-1,1]$:
$$E_n(r) \;=\; \min_{b_0,b_1,\dots,b_{n-2}\in\mathbb{R}} \; \max_{x\in[-1,1]} \; \bigl|\, x^n + r\,x^{n-1} - (b_0 + b_1 x + b_2 x^2 + \cdots + b_{n-2} x^{n-2})\,\bigr|.$$
That is, given the leading two terms $x^n + r x^{n-1}$, find the polynomial $B(x) = b_0 + b_1 x + \cdots + b_{n-2} x^{n-2}$ of degree at most $n-2$ that best approximates $x^n + r x^{n-1}$ in the uniform (sup) norm on $[-1,1]$.

The task is, working in the first-order theory of the real numbers, to perform quantifier elimination on the formula expressing the optimal value $E_n(r)$ and the optimal coefficients $b_0,\dots,b_{n-2}$ as functions of $r$, and to obtain by computer an explicit closed-form (semi-algebraic) description of the optimal $B$ and of $E_n(r)$ for $n \ge 6$. Equivalently, produce explicit algebraic expressions (as piecewise algebraic functions of $r$) for the coefficients $b_i(r)$ of the best approximant and for the minimax error.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem (often called Zolotarev's / Solotareff's problem, posed as a quantifier-elimination challenge by Collins in 1992) has been solved by general quantifier-elimination tools (e.g., qepcad) only for small degrees: a complete explicit semi-algebraic solution is known for n ≤ 4, and partial results (e.g., explicit form for n = 5, where the associated relation curve has genus 1) have been obtained via algebraic-geometric methods using curve parametrization. For general n ≥ 6, no complete closed-form solution by quantifier elimination has been reported; the problem remains a challenge benchmark.

status_evidence.title: An Algebraic-Geometric Method for Computing Zolotarev Polynomials
status_evidence.snippet: qepcad was used to successfully compute the coefficients for n ≤ 4, and also compute the coefficients for n = 5 for fixed values of r; for n=5 the reduced relation curve has genus 1.
status_evidence.claim: Explicit QE-based solutions are known only for n ≤ 4, with partial progress for n = 5; n ≥ 6 not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Application of Quantifier Elimination to Solotareff's Approximation Problem (Collins)
status_evidence.snippet: Collins applied quantifier elimination to Solotareff's best polynomial approximation problem.
status_evidence.claim: The problem was posed and partially attacked by Collins via QE.
